question: Kesar Valley Foods Pvt Ltd, a fictional family-owned snack maker, has steady profits but plans a large new plant in two years. A private equity fund wants to buy a 30% stake and has asked the promoters for a valuation. The promoters' advisor has proposed using only the book value of net assets. Advise the promoters on suitable valuation approaches and the key judgements involved.
sources: ICAI Valuation Standards 2018 - ICAI Valuation Standard 103 Valuation Approaches and Methods
Ind AS 113 Fair Value Measurement - valuation techniques

points.label: Book value alone is not suitable
points.description: Net asset book value ignores future earnings, the new plant, brands and goodwill, so it would understate the value of a profitable going concern; it is better used as a floor or cross-check.
points.basis: ICAI Valuation Standard 103: cost/asset approach and when it is appropriate

points.label: Income approach
points.description: A discounted cash flow valuation of free cash flows, including the planned plant and its funding, discounted at a rate reflecting the business's risk, suits a growing profitable company.

points.label: Market approach
points.description: Multiples (such as EV/EBITDA or P/E) of comparable listed companies or recent deals, adjusted for size, growth and the lack of a listing, give a market-based check.

points.label: Key judgements
points.description: Reliability of the promoters' projections, the discount rate and terminal growth, and choice of comparables; results from different methods are reconciled and weighted with reasons.
points.basis: ICAI Valuation Standard 103: selecting and weighting approaches

points.label: Stake-specific factors
points.description: A 30% non-controlling stake may attract a discount for lack of control and marketability, offset by investor protection rights; the valuation base and date should be stated in the report.
points.basis: ICAI Valuation Standards: valuation bases and premise; general valuation practice on control and marketability
